newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban claim gains against opposition in Kunar.
newsitem.headline: Taleban claim gains against opposition in Kunar.

text.p: Afghanistan's fundamentalist Islamic Taleban militia said on Sunday it had recaptured the town of Asmar, in the northeastern province of Kunar, from opposition forces.

Maulvi Sadr Azam, governor of the Taleban-held eastern city of Jalalabad, told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press service that Taleban forces had seized Asmar, about 110 km (69 miles) northeast of Jalalabad, on Saturday night.
Azam said the Taleban were pursuing their foes into the hills, but had regained full control of Kunar province after an anti-Taleban rebellion there early this month.
Some reports say the uprising began when the Taleban tried to disarm local tribesman. Others link it to a Taleban crackdown on smuggling of timber into neighbouring Pakistan.
Azam said the rebels, led by Malik Zareen Khan, were backed by the former shura (council) of neutral factions controlling Nangahar province, of which Jalalabad is the capital.
Azam said more than 40 people had been killed in clashes with the rebels this month, including a Taleban leader named Maulvi Kaleemullah, in charge of education in Nangarhar.
Azam said the Taleban crushed a similar revolt in the Pech Pass area of Kunar in mid-1996, which also cost about 40 dead.
The Taleban, who captured the capital Kabul on September 27, are trying to impose their strict version of Islam across the country. They already control more than 75 percent of Afghanistan.

Their attempts to advance into northern provinces are opposed by a coalition that includes forces loyal to the former government of Burhanuddin Rabbani, ethnic Uzbek military leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum and a Shi'ite Moslem faction.
